chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) of my need and asked him to teach me a supplication for seeking sustenance, so he taught me a supplication, and I did not remain in need since I supplicated with it.
He said: Say it at the end of the night prayer.

And you are in prostration: O best of those supplicated to, and O best of those asked from, and O most extensive of those who give, and O best of those hoped from! Grant me sustenance and expand upon me from Your sustenance, and provide for me a means of sustenance from Yourself. Indeed, You are Able over all things.
ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication for seeking sustenance taught by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the efficacy of supplicating during the humble state of prostration (sajdah) after the night prayer (Salat al-Layl), a time of divine proximity. The Imam’s assurance that he never needed it again underscores the spiritual potency of this specific invocation for securing sustenance (rizq) through divine generosity.
